output.brief: Pellacott's valves built in 2026 are the problem, not the installers or the firmware. Claim rates are the same across legacy and new installers (41 vs 42 per 1,000) and across firmware 4.1 and 4.2 (40 vs 42). Durrant-Hale valves stay low (5–7) in every group. Warehouse valves that were never installed leak at the seat in 11% of Pellacott 2026 lots, against 1% for 2025 and 0% for Durrant-Hale. The teardowns show a deformed, unseated slide seal. The leak test certificates are not credible. Pellacott's test rig has been out of service since January 2026, and no VA-220 test program is loaded on the other rigs. The 2026 per-piece tables repeat four sequences that already appear in November 2025 certificates. The score rose because it rewards complete certificates, not tested parts. Next steps: do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott stock and suspend dock-to-stock. Release stock only after Brenmoor's own helium test. Drop the installer remediation plan and chargebacks. Fix the scoring so it needs rig logs or witnessed tests. Check other suppliers' records. The Corlin seal and Line 3 effects cannot yet be separated, so don't mandate a seal change yet. I'm fairly confident in this.
